text.en: The ones who come back from the maze all wear the same face. Nobody asks what it means.
text.ja: 迷宮から戻ってくる連中は、みんな同じ顔をしてるよ。

text.en: Guests upstairs always line their boots up neatly before bed, like soldiers who've been told to.
text.ja: 二階の客は、寝る前に必ず靴をきちんと揃えるんだ。

text.en: The temple's donation box keeps getting lighter, and nobody will say why.
text.ja: 寺院の寄付箱が、このところ軽くなる一方でね。

text.en: The shopkeeper gives a long lecture to anyone buying a sword, and only to them.
text.ja: 店の親父は、剣を買う客にだけ長々と説教するんだ。

text.en: Newcomers dying within three days has been a rule for as long as anyone can remember.
text.ja: 新顔が三日で死ぬのは、昔からの決まりみたいなもんさ。

text.en: The corner table in here is always empty. Nobody sits there, and nobody says why.
text.ja: 酒場の隅の席は、いつも空いてる。座る奴がいないんだ。

text.en: The men back from the maze buy candles like they're going out of style. Turns out they like the light.
text.ja: 迷宮帰りの連中は、やたら蝋燭を買い込むね。明るいのが好きらしい。

text.en: Someone leaves the same wilted flowers at the maze entrance every morning. Nobody claims them.
text.ja: 迷宮の入口に、誰かが毎朝同じ花を供えてるんだ。

text.en: Dead men always come home wearing their Sunday best, or so the widow tells anyone who'll listen.
text.ja: 死んだ男は、みんな一番いい服を着て帰ってくるらしいよ。

text.en: A peddler's cart creaked outside the town all night, and by morning the peddler was gone.
text.ja: 行商の荷車が、町の外で一晩中きしんでたって話だ。

text.en: The apprentice has been sighing all week. Love, the barkeep says. Or the dungeon. Same thing, mostly.
text.ja: 修行中の見習いが、最近ため息ばかりついてる。恋でもしたかね。

text.en: Anyone who buys a new shield comes crying back within a week. Mostly they want it refitted.
text.ja: 盾を新品で買うやつは、たいてい一週間で泣きついてくるよ。

text.en: The shop that sells adventurers' leftovers is doing well, which tells you something about the town.
text.ja: 冒険者の遺品を売る店は、なぜか儲かってるんだ。

text.en: The temple's sexton counts something every night, muttering under his breath. Nobody has asked what.
text.ja: 寺院の寺男は、毎晩ぶつぶつ数を数えてるよ。

text.en: The maze door is found a little open most mornings. Everyone says it's the wind. Nobody believes it.
text.ja: 迷宮の扉が、朝になると少し開いてるんだと。風のせいだとさ。

text.en: The best adventurer in town finally skipped out on her inn bill. The barkeep is taking it personally.
text.ja: 一番腕のいい冒険者が、とうとう宿代を踏み倒したってさ。

text.en: Nobody pays the town bell any mind anymore. They only get loud when it fails to ring.
text.ja: 町の鐘なんて、もう誰も気にしないよ。鳴り損ねた時だけ騒ぐ。

text.en: The temple priest grumbles that prayers aren't working as well lately. He blames the candles.
text.ja: 祈りの効きが悪いって、寺院の坊主が愚痴ってたよ。

text.en: The price of ale only goes up, and the customers' faces only go down. Business is business.
text.ja: 酒の値は上がる一方なのに、客の顔色は下がる一方だ。

text.en: The travelling bard came through but refused to sing anything about the maze. Said it doesn't pay.
text.ja: 旅の詩人が来たが、迷宮の歌だけは絶対歌わないんだ。

text.en: The laundress has been burning the clothes of returning adventurers. She won't say why, and nobody asks.
text.ja: 洗濯女が、帰ってきた冒険者の服を焼いてるのを見たって。

text.en: Writing a will before going into the maze is the fashionable thing now. The notary is doing a brisk trade.
text.ja: 迷宮に入る前に遺言を書くのは、もう流行りの作法らしい。

text.en: Local kids play at the maze and all say the same line. Nobody taught it to them. That's the creepy part.
text.ja: 子どもが迷宮ごっこで、みんな同じ台詞を言うんだ。気味が悪い。

text.en: The innkeeper's wife insists smokers live longer. She has been insisting for forty years.
text.ja: 煙草を吸う奴は長生きするって、宿の婆さんが言い張るんだよ。

text.en: The well water tastes of iron this season. The barkeep says that's just what the town tastes like.
text.ja: 井戸の水が鉄くさいのは今年だけだと、酒場の親父が言い張る。

text.en: Inspect a chest before you open it. Once you know the trap's name, disarming it is far easier.
text.ja: 宝箱は、開ける前に調べておけ。罠の名前が分かれば、外すのもずっと楽になる。

text.en: Leave the disarming to someone with thieves' tools. Bare hands are a poor bet.
text.ja: 罠を外すなら、盗賊道具を持った奴にやらせるんだな。素手じゃ分が悪い。

text.en: Kill one of an unknown creature and you'll know what they are. A sharp-witted friend may see through them at a glance.
text.ja: 正体の分からん化け物も、一匹倒せば何者か分かる。頭のいい仲間なら、見ただけで見抜くこともある。

text.en: A short rest in the maze isn't only for wounds. Rest in peace and someone may work out what that unknown find really is.
text.ja: 迷宮で一休みするなら、手当てだけじゃない。無事に休めた奴は、拾った品の正体を見極めることがある。

text.en: Don't wander around poisoned. Every step wears you down.
text.ja: 毒をもらったまま歩き回るな。一歩ごとに体が削れていく。

text.en: Short of coin? Sleep in the stable. You only get half your strength back, but your spells and skills return by morning.
text.ja: 懐が寂しいなら馬小屋で寝な。体は半分しか戻らんが、呪文も技も朝には戻ってる。

text.en: One night at the inn restores all your Hit Dice, wherever you sleep. Don't fret about spending them on short rests below.
text.ja: 宿で一晩寝れば、休むための力(ヒットダイス)はどこで寝ても全部戻る。迷宮での小休憩で使い切っても気にするな。

text.en: The first three in line stand in front. Keep your spellcasters at the back.
text.ja: 並びの前の三人が前に立つ。呪文使いは後ろに下げときな。

text.en: Named monsters either keep a lair or roam. Beat one and they say it drops something fine.
text.ja: 名のある化け物は、ねぐらを構えるか、うろつくかだ。倒せば、いい品を落とすって話さ。

text.en: Friends left down in the maze can be brought back by another party. Don't give up on them yet.
text.ja: 迷宮に置いてきた仲間は、別の一行を組めば連れ戻せる。見捨てるのはまだ早い。

text.en: Even a plain wall can be worth searching. That's where hidden doors tend to be.
text.ja: 壁に見えても、調べてみる価値はある。隠し扉ってのは、そういう所にあるもんだ。

text.en: Some floors turn you around without you noticing. If your map looks wrong, suspect one of those.
text.ja: 気づかんうちに向きを変えられる床がある。地図がおかしいと思ったら、そいつを疑え。

text.en: They say there are places where no spell will work. Parties that lean on magic, take care.
text.ja: 呪文が一切使えん場所もあるそうだ。呪文頼みの一行は気をつけな。

text.en: Get unfamiliar finds identified at the shop. Once you've put on something cursed, it's too late.
text.ja: 見たことのない品は、店で鑑定してもらえ。呪われた物を身につけてからじゃ遅い。

text.en: Running from a fight you can't win is a fair choice. Much cheaper than the temple bringing you back.
text.ja: 勝てん相手からは逃げるのも手だ。死んで寺院の世話になるより、ずっと安くつく。
